correctness.rationale: Averaging over core–leaf pair permutations preserves symmetric stochastic support and cannot increase the convex centered operator norm. Constants on the layers give 1 and 1−2b; mean-zero pairs give a repeated 2×2 block with larger root 1−b−ma/2+sqrt(b²+(ma/2)²). For 0<b<1 that root strictly decreases in a, so its lower envelope in the feasible triangle occurs at a=(1−b)/(m−1). In t=b/(1−b) its derivative has the sign of (t−c²)/sqrt(t²+c²)−d, strictly increasing from −1 to c. The zero is (c+d sqrt(2c))/(2−c), and stationarity gives the optimum s by s=d+c sqrt(1−s²). At these weights 0<b<1/2 and the contrast-block trace is positive for m≥3, so neither the other contrast root nor the layer root exceeds s in modulus. b=0 or b=1 gives SLEM one. The strict inequalities for the lower envelope yield invariant uniqueness only. For a=b=1/m the same comparisons apply, and the root gives the quoted heuristic formula; its gap is 1/m+O(m^−2), whereas the optimal gap tends to 1/5. At m=2, b=a=1/2, the two extreme roots tie at modulus 1/sqrt(2), consistent with the known path endpoint. The supplied spectral checker and recorded run were inspected, not executed; the exact argument does not rely on the random competitors.
